The Commonwealth of Massachusetts Office of the Secretary
Massachusells Historical Commission 294 Washington Street Boston, Massachusetts 02108
[617] 727-8470
July 1, 1977
Mr. Marvin Siflinger Acting Area Office Director Department of Housing and Urban Development 15 New Chardon Street Boston, MA 02114
Attn: Environmental Clearance Officer
Re: Kendall Square Urban Renewal: Draft EIS
Dear Mr. Siflinger:
The Massachusetts Historical Commission has reviewed the Draft EIS and would like to make the following comments.
The Draft EIS's discussion of historical and archeological resources in the context of aesthetics (Ch.II-4) adequately deals with our concerns. We concur with the finding of no impact on any known or eligible National Register properties in the project impact area (Ch.II-4-14).
From an historical viewpoint the three "Build" alternatives are more appropriate than a park use as they far more clearly reflect the historical development of the area as an importnat industrial, commercial and trading section of Cambridge.
The measures to minimize adverse effects on the environment (Ch.II-4-17) are satisfactory in terms of the project's relationship to historic resources. Regarding #3. Use of materials to highlight historic development, we recommend that the Cambridge Historical Commission be consulted to review and suggest appropriate historic treatments.
We are pleased to see that the efforts to minimize adverse impacts will help to visually relate the new development to its surroundings. This viewpoint can and should be encouraged as it will lead to a design concept reflective of continuing urban revitalization and sensitive to the urban qualities which define Kendall Square.
ANEW DINCHARA Elizabeth Red athers But 5 mg
Elizabeth Reed Amadon
Executive Director, Massachusetts Historical Commission
